answers.change_2023_2026: There have been right protections both in 2023 and 2026 and neither the right protection nor the implementation level of these protections has changed

provisions.instrument: Decreto 177 de 2022 (Ministerio del Interior), subcategorías de residencia temporal

answers.implementation_then_now: Around 2023 the reunification permit, in force since May 2022, was being granted in large numbers, but against a backlog SERMIG puts at about 600,000 pending applications in March 2022 (386,024 in December 2022). By early 2026 SERMIG was granting almost 40,000 reunification permits a year (2025). Of 28,584 applications pending in January 2026, only 3% of those decided had been rejected. Delays persist: courts of appeal (Temuco 2024, Antofagasta 2024, San Miguel 2026) ordered SERMIG to decide applications that had been stalled, and the Haitian community reports waits of more than two years. Applications are honoured in the main with long delays. I see no documented shift between the two dates, so I keep the starting rating.

¿Cómo opera la reunificación familiar en Chile? (La Tercera)

answers.sourcing_note: The LeyChile consolidated JSON tags each amended article with the amending act and its Diario Oficial date. Art. 19 and Art. 74 of Ley 21.325 carry no amendment tag, and Decreto 177/2022 carries none at all. Every amendment to Ley 21.325 (Leyes 21.589, 21.590, 21.610, 21.655, 21.730, 21.816) touches other articles. Ley 20.430 was not reopened. The SERMIG and Defensoría de la Niñez PDFs could not be read (no PDF extractor), so the practice evidence comes from the press quoting SERMIG data.

sources_opened.title: La Tercera, Cómo opera la reunificación familiar

answers.starting_answer_concern: The 'Yes' is defensible for spouses, parents, minor or disabled children and students under 24. But the list in Art. 19 and Decreto 177 Art. 12 is closed: non-dependent adult relatives are excluded. The reunification permit itself is open only to relatives of Chileans and of permanent ('definitiva') residents. Temporary residents can bring only spouses and children, as dependants with an income requirement (Ley 21.325 Art. 74; Decreto 177 Art. 72). On the MRD's own Colombia example this looks closer to 'Conditional'. The implementation evidence (large backlogs, waits of two years or more) fits 'Usually' better than 'Usually; Effectively Always'.
answers.notes: Protection answer rests on the statutes (Ley 21.325 Art. 19; Decreto 177 Arts. 12-16), not on case law. The Ley 20.430 provisions the MRD cites were not reread. Leyes 21.730 (D.O. 05.02.2025) and 21.816 (D.O. 02.06.2026) amended Arts. 1 and 88 of Ley 21.325, not the family provisions. In November 2026 SERMIG said it was updating its regulations with more controls on reunification, after the window. Bills on reunification (Boletines 18614-06, 18377-06, 17511-06) were pending, not enacted.

answers.change_2023_2026: There have been right protections both in 2023 and 2026 and neither the right protection nor the implementation level of these protections has changed

provisions.article: Art. 139 (administrative remedies under Ley 19.880 'sin perjuicio de los demás recursos y acciones judiciales')

answers.implementation_then_now: In both periods the courts of appeal hear recursos de protección and amparo against SERMIG decisions and delays, and often grant them. Examples: CA Temuco Rol 12632-2023 (Feb 2024, six-month delay on a reunification visa); CA Antofagasta Roles 1750-2024 and 1935-2024 (2024); CA Valparaíso Rol 5319-2025 (Dec 2025, residence delay, not reunification). After the window, in March 2026, the Corte Suprema quashed a rejection and ordered SERMIG to reconsider under the reunification subcategory, applying Art. 19. Limits: the Supreme Court has held that amparo is not the route to speed up procedures, and some courts treat protección as unsuited to mere expectations. The remedy works in the main, with known gaps. I see no shift between the two dates.

answers.sourcing_note: In the LeyChile JSON, Constitution Art. 20 was last modified by Ley 20.516 (D.O. 11.07.2011). Ley 21.325 Arts. 139-141 carry no amendment tags. The in-window reunification rulings (Temuco, Antofagasta) are known only from search results; their PDFs could not be opened, so they are not relied on as read.
answers.starting_answer_concern: The MRD cites Ley 21.325 Art. 169, which sets out consular functions abroad and has nothing to do with remedies. The relevant provisions are Art. 139 (Ley 19.880 administrative appeals 'sin perjuicio de los demás recursos y acciones judiciales que procedan') and Constitution Art. 20 (protección). The only specific judicial appeal in the statute, Art. 141, covers expulsion only. The 'Conditional' therefore turns on the absence of a dedicated statutory judicial appeal against reunification refusals.
answers.notes: Protection answer rests on the Constitution and statutes, not on a ruling. The court decisions are used as practice evidence only, read through Diario Constitucional reports, not the full judgments.

answers.change_2023_2026: There have been right protections both in 2023 and 2026 and neither the right protection nor the implementation level of these protections has changed

provisions.instrument: Ley 21.400 (matrimonio entre personas del mismo sexo)

answers.implementation_then_now: Art. 19 of Ley 21.325 and Art. 12 a) of Decreto 177 cover the 'cónyuge' or an equivalent relationship (including civil union). Since Ley 21.400, which amended Código Civil Art. 102 ('dos personas') and Art. 31 (references apply 'a todos los cónyuges, sin distinción de sexo'), this includes same-sex spouses. La Tercera (2026) quotes practitioners who list the cónyuge or conviviente civil among the qualifying links. I found no documented refusal of same-sex spouses in either period, but also no specific practice data on them. I keep the starting rating for both dates.

answers.change_2023_2026: There have been right protections both in 2023 and 2026 and neither the right protection nor the implementation level of these protections has changed
answers.implementation_then_now: The reunification permit for relatives of Chileans and permanent residents (Decreto 177 Arts. 12-16) asks only for proof of the family link, a criminal record certificate and, for minors, custody papers. It has no income test, and the practitioners quoted by La Tercera (2026) list no resource requirement. SERMIG granted almost 40,000 such permits in 2025 and rejected about 3% of applications decided. Dependants of temporary residents must show the sponsor has stable income. I see no documented shift between the two dates.

answers.sourcing_note: The relevant articles of Ley 21.325 (19, 74) carry no amendment tags in LeyChile, and Decreto 177 carries none at all, so the text was the same on both dates. Practice evidence is press reporting of SERMIG data, mostly from 2025-2026; I found little from 2022-2023.

sources_opened.title: La Tercera, Cómo opera la reunificación familiar

answers.starting_answer_concern: The 'Yes' holds only for the reunification permit sponsored by Chileans or permanent residents. Temporary residents bringing a spouse or children as dependants must meet a resource condition. Ley 21.325 Art. 74 says 'El titular deberá acreditar actividad económica o ingresos estables que permitan la manutención de quienes postulen a la residencia temporal en calidad de dependientes suyos', and Decreto 177 Art. 72 repeats it. The indicator is binary, so a stricter coder could answer 'No' for migrants generally.
answers.notes: Protection answer rests on the statutes and decree only. None of the amending laws 21.589, 21.590, 21.610, 21.655, 21.730 or 21.816 touched Arts. 19 or 74.
